skill.displayName: Pet Grooming Effectiveness & Hairball Risk Analysis | 宠物梳毛器梳理效果与毛球风险

llm.summary: The skill performs the stated pet grooming analysis, but it also silently creates or reuses an identity, stores tokens locally, and queries cloud history, so it needs Review before install.

dimensions.detail: The skill reads local media files, sends local files or URLs to remote APIs, derives workspace data paths, and can read a workspace identity file; these are partly purpose-aligned but not tightly user-controlled.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time script or destructive setup was found; the package uses Python scripts and ordinary requirements files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The manifest instructs automatic cloud history queries and internal identity handling without asking the user for identity or separate confirmation before using that identity.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The common utilities create a workspace SQLite database, create or reuse a default user, read data/smyx-api-key.txt, silently register/login with a remote service, and persist returned tokens/open tokens.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Remote pet-media analysis and cloud history lookup are documented, but automatic account bootstrap, identity reuse, token storage, and history access are high-impact capabilities that exceed a simple one-shot analysis workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with pet media or media URLs being sent to the provider's cloud service and with the skill silently creating/reusing an account identity, storing authentication tokens in the workspace data directory, and using that identity to retrieve prior cloud reports. Review or remove the automatic identity/login and history features if you only need one-time media analysis.
llm.findings:
[AST7] expected: Verified dynamic getattr filtering in the generic DAO; no current entrypoint was found that passes user-controlled filter keys into those methods, so this is a hardening issue rather than a verdict driver.
[LP3] unexpected: The manifest discloses local files and server APIs, but the runtime also performs identity resolution, token persistence, authenticated requests, and cloud history access without a clear least-privilege permission boundary.
[SDI-1] expected: History report listing is documented in SKILL.md and the API reference, so listing itself is purpose-aligned; the concern is the breadth of supporting account and persistence behavior.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted in part: automatic default-user creation and account/token persistence in the shared workspace data directory broaden the skill beyond pure media analysis.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted: open_id checks are commented out for analysis and listing while the entrypoint resolves a current/default identity, so prior cloud reports may be returned for whichever identity is silently selected.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted: broad automatic triggers for history-report phrases can initiate a cloud report query without a separate confirmation step.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted: remote media/URL processing is disclosed, but local credential-file use, auth header attachment, and silent remote account bootstrap are not presented as a user-controlled consent step.
[E1] unexpected: Accepted: the request helper can send openId, mobile, and source to a health login endpoint with silent registration enabled, which is not necessary for a one-shot media analysis request.
[P2] expected: Downgraded: the Unicode-format matches observed in SKILL.md are zero-width joiners in emoji; the Markdown report instruction should sanitize API-returned links, but no artifact-backed prompt injection was found.
[YR4] expected: Downgraded: the frontmatter contains a long operational description and emoji-related hidden characters, but no evaluator-directed metadata poisoning instructions were found.
